answer: Agents can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits show duplicated or fabricated results. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital in each fake account, while honest agents recover their deposits; creating identities is no longer free. A lagoon of low-cost accounts cannot amplify a signal without risking funds, and the audit process becomes an oasis of evidence for distinguishing costly participation from mere headcount.
